Google is retiring the standalone Local Services Ads dashboard and folding it into Google Ads as a specialized Performance Max campaign.

If you're a plumber, HVAC company, electrician, roofer, or run any home service business using Local Services Ads, this affects you starting this month.

The good news: pay per lead, Search and Maps only placement, and keywordless targeting all stay exactly the same. What's changing is the dashboard itself, manual bidding, how budgets are structured, and the BBB callout.

The one thing worth doing now, whether or not you've gotten a migration notice yet: export your historical performance reports. Google's own documentation says they will not transfer automatically.

Full breakdown, including a question I keep seeing come up that Google hasn't actually answered yet: https://brightboxdigital.io/blog/local-services-ads-moving-to-google-ads/

Google is moving Local Services Ads into Google Ads.

For home service businesses running LSA, here's what's actually changing this month: the standalone dashboard is being retired, manual bidding goes away, weekly budgets convert to daily averages, and Better Business Bureau callouts are no longer supported.

What isn't changing: you still only pay for a real lead, ads still show exclusively on Search and Maps, and the campaign stays keywordless.

Migration starts in August 2026 for home and storefront service categories (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, appliance repair, house cleaning, lawn care, roofing, pest control, and moving), then expands through 2027.

The one thing worth doing regardless of your migration date: export your historical performance reports now. Google's documentation states plainly that past impressions, clicks, spend, and ad-level reports will not transfer automatically. Lead history will, but the reporting context around it will not.

I also address a question I've seen come up repeatedly that Google's documentation does not directly resolve: whether this new campaign type competes with an existing standard Performance Max campaign for budget. Worth reading if you're running both.
